decisions.reason: The candidate already requires easy bowl removal and swapping; using removability as a possible cleaning method does not change that behavior.
The cleaning decision does not alter bowl capacity, form, size, or refilling preferences.
Ease of cleaning or removal does not establish any change to the required food-contact material.
The source message separately modifies dispensing flow, and that same-message Event is already present; the cleaning change does not further alter flow quality.
The source message separately modifies splash control, and that Event is already present; bowl and spout cleanability does not change the splash-control state.
The cleaning decision does not resolve or modify the independently ambiguous whisk-head configuration.
The source message separately refines mixing quality, and that Event is already present; cleanability does not alter the desired mixing result.
Making spout components easy to clean or removable does not necessarily change the spout's location, orientation, geometry, or fabrication style.
The cleanability decision does not change solenoid actuation or valve-control behavior, and the source merely retains the already-selected solenoid approach.
The source reiterates existing no-drip and no-leak constraints, while the cleaning change adds no new liquid-containment state.
Requiring cleanable or removable bowls and spout components does not necessarily change the V1 sourcing or custom-fabrication strategy.
The cleanability requirement does not change the existence or defined content of the system-layout deliverable.
